newsitem.title: GERMANY: Some signs of move out of the mark - Buba member.
newsitem.headline: Some signs of move out of the mark - Buba member.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen has said he has seen some signs that investors were transferring funds out of the mark ahead of Europe's planned monetary union but there were no indications of major shifts.
"There are no signs of a large wave, but there are signs," Jochimsen told reporters at a dinner on Wednesday evening.
He said he was referring to investors transferring funds into the perceived safe havens of the British pound sterling, Swiss franc and U.S. dollar.
Jochimsen said the mark had already normalised following its sharp appreciation against the dollar and other currencies in 1995.
"The mark normalisation is there, we must closely watch it," he said.

Jochimsen said it was impossible to make a safe prediction regarding exchange rates because they depended on a number of factors, including whether Japan would raise interest rates and whether U.S. interest rates would rise further.
Jochimsen is president of the state central bank of North Rhine-Westphalia.
